subject: MGMT464
title: Hurdle 8 · The Collapsing Tunnel — Strategic Leadership and Change Management

questions.stem: Describe strategic leadership.
options: The ability to anticipate, envision, maintain flexibility and empower others to create strategic change
The process of formulating and implementing strategies
questions.why: Strategic leadership vs strategic management. See §8.1.

questions.stem: Identify the five strategic decision categories in order.
options: Vision and mission; objectives; strategy formulation; strategy execution; evaluation and control
questions.why: The map. See §8.1.

questions.stem: Explain what the strategic leader adds beyond analysis.
options: Anticipation of change, a vision people commit to, flexibility to adjust, and empowerment of others to execute
questions.why: Analysts can do the analysis. See §8.1.

questions.stem: Explain how Google's strategy came to fit its culture, in the chapter's reading.
options: The leaders built both — they made change the culture by what they rewarded and how fast ideas were tested
questions.why: Answer to question 1. See §8.1.

questions.stem: Describe a vision.
options: An ambitious view of the future everyone can believe in, not readily attainable, yet better in important ways
The organisation's core purpose and reason for existence
A measurable target with a date
questions.why: Vision. See §8.2.

questions.stem: Describe a mission.
options: The organisation's core broad purpose — what we do, for whom, and what makes us distinct
An ambitious picture of the future
questions.why: Mission. See §8.2.

questions.stem: Identify a criterion of an effective vision.
options: Clear, simple and memorable — one sentence a new employee repeats
questions.why: Criteria for a vision. See §8.2.

questions.stem: Identify the Chapter 6 link for the vision.
options: The vision is stage 2 of the transformation process — the transformational leader makes it shared; the strategic leader makes it operational
The vision is a transactional exchange
questions.why: The Chapter 6 link. See §8.2.

questions.stem: Differentiate objectives from strategies.
options: Objectives are the ends (what, by when); strategies are the means (how)
Objectives are the means; strategies are the ends
questions.why: Objectives say what; strategies say how. See §8.3.

questions.stem: Identify the textbook's rule about objectives and strategies.
options: An objective without a strategy is a wish, and a strategy without an objective is activity
questions.why: The rule. See §8.3.

questions.stem: Describe how objectives cascade.
options: The organisation's objective becomes each unit's objective becomes each person's — the alignment execution depends on
questions.why: Objectives cascade. See §8.3.

questions.stem: Explain why the 'beautiful strategy' in question 2 changed nothing.
options: There were no objectives at the department level — nobody had a number to reach
questions.why: Answer to question 2, first part. See §8.3.

questions.stem: Describe strategy formulation.
options: Matching what the organisation CAN do (internal analysis) with what the environment WILL reward (external analysis)
questions.why: Why analysis comes before the plan. See §8.4.

questions.stem: Identify what the external analysis examines.
options: Industry and competition, customers, technology, regulation and policy, economic conditions, the labour market
questions.why: Opportunities and threats. See §8.4.

questions.stem: Explain why formulation is a leadership act.
options: It requires judgement under uncertainty and the courage to choose, which no analysis supplies
Only leaders can read SWOT tables
questions.why: Formulation — the strategic leader's choice. See §8.4.

questions.stem: Explain what made Google's search-and-ads strategy leadership rather than analysis.
options: Betting the company on it before the evidence was complete
questions.why: The Google case. See §8.4.

questions.stem: Identify the six things execution requires.
options: Structure aligned, culture aligned, resources allocated, leadership at every level, communication and commitment, measurement and correction
A video, a poster, a memo, a party, a bonus, a logo
Vision, mission, values, slogan, website, app
Budget, budget, budget, budget, budget, budget
questions.why: Where most strategies die. See §8.5.

questions.stem: Describe what goes wrong with 'new strategy, old structure'.
options: The departments still optimise the old goals
questions.why: Execution requires structure aligned. See §8.5.

questions.stem: Explain the textbook's blunt point about formulation and execution.
options: Formulation is the easier part; most strategies fail in execution
questions.why: Blunt. See §8.5.

questions.stem: Explain why the town-hall video in question 2 failed.
options: Execution needs six elements; the video covered one
questions.why: Answer to question 2, second part. See §8.5.

questions.stem: Identify the external forces for change.
options: Technology, competition, customers, regulation, economic shocks
Growth, new leadership, performance gaps, culture drift
questions.why: External forces. See §8.6.

questions.stem: Identify the strategic leader's role in change.
options: Anticipate, create urgency, build a shared vision, form a coalition, empower, generate short-term wins, consolidate, institutionalise
questions.why: The textbook's list. See §8.6.

questions.stem: Differentiate incremental from transformational change.
options: Incremental: continuous improvement inside the current strategy, led transactionally; transformational: a new strategy, structure or culture, led transformationally
questions.why: Two kinds of change, two kinds of leadership. See §8.6.

questions.stem: Explain why strategy is 'only paper'.
options: Until people change what they do — and getting people to change is leadership work, not project management
questions.why: Every strategy is a change. See §8.6.

questions.stem: Identify Lewin's three phases.
questions.why: Lewin's model. See §8.7.

questions.stem: Describe refreezing.
options: Stabilising the new state — aligning rewards, structure, culture and measurement so it does not slide back; the phase most leaders skip
questions.why: Why change 'didn't stick'. See §8.7.

questions.stem: Identify the textbook's practical rule in force-field analysis.
options: Reducing a restraining force moves the situation with less stress than adding driving force
Add as much pressure as possible
questions.why: Adding pressure raises tension and resistance. See §8.7.

questions.stem: Identify examples of restraining forces.
options: Habit, fear of loss, skills gap, sunk investment, a culture that rewards the old way
New regulation, customer demand, a competitor
questions.why: Restraining forces. See §8.7.

questions.stem: Explain the chapter's stance on resistance.
options: Treat resistance as information — it tells you what the change plan is missing; treat it as disloyalty and it hardens
questions.why: Resistance is information. See §8.8.

questions.stem: Identify the recommendation for 'uncertainty and fear of the unknown'.
options: Communicate early, often and specifically; training before go-live; pilots
Show what they gain; compensate real losses
Respect the expertise and give time
questions.why: Uncertainty. See §8.8.

questions.stem: Identify the recommendation for 'habit, inertia and sunk investment'.
options: Respect the expertise, use it in the design, give time and support to relearn
questions.why: Habit. See §8.8.

questions.stem: Explain how to reach the silent resisters in questions 3 and 4.
options: Reach them individually, respect the expertise, pair them with a peer, make the first success visible — the silent one you must involve
questions.why: The loud resister you can argue with. See §8.8.

questions.stem: Exercise 1A: 'We will be the most trusted healthcare provider in the Northern Emirates.' Classify the statement.
questions.why: Answer key: A vision. See §8.2 and Exercise 1.

questions.stem: Exercise 1B: 'Reduce patient no-shows from 18% to 10% by June 2027 through SMS reminders and a same-day rebooking line.' Classify the statement.
options: An objective, with a strategy embedded
questions.why: Answer key: B objective with strategy. See §8.3 and Exercise 1.

questions.stem: Exercise 1C: 'Improve customer service.' Classify it and select the rewrite in the textbook's format.
options: A wish — 'To raise first-contact resolution from 60% to 80% by 31 December 2027'
questions.why: Answer key: C wish → measurable objective. See §8.3 and Exercise 1.

questions.stem: Exercise 1D: a ministry announces all services will be digital within two years; front-desk staff have twenty years' experience with paper. Determine the driving force, the restraining force and what is protected.
options: Driving: the national digital strategy; restraining: skill and habit, fear of incompetence — protecting competence
Driving: staff; restraining: the minister — protecting pay
Driving: paper; restraining: digital — protecting status
Driving: fear; restraining: strategy — protecting belonging
questions.why: Answer key: D protecting competence. See §8.7, §8.8 and Exercise 1.

questions.stem: Exercise 1E: a competitor launches same-day delivery; riders paid per parcel fear the routing app will cut their income. Determine the reason for resistance and what it protects.
options: Fear of the unknown — protecting certainty
questions.why: Answer key: E threat to self-interest. See §8.8 and Exercise 1.

questions.stem: Exercise 1F: a dean introduces a new assessment system; the two most respected professors quietly keep their old exams. Determine the restraining forces and the recommendation — and the response that would harden it.
options: Habit, distrust and sunk expertise — involve them in designing the system and respect the expertise; a public reprimand would harden it and pull the department with them
Fear of pay loss — compensate; a bonus would harden it
Lack of conviction — show data; a pilot would harden it
Peer pressure — ignore them; involvement would harden it
questions.why: Answer key: F involve the informal leaders. See §8.8 and Exercise 1.

questions.stem: Exercise 2: the logistics company's digital warehouse system serves the e-commerce strategy. Select the objective in the textbook's format.
options: 'To process 100% of warehouse transactions in the digital system by 30 June 2027 while holding cost per parcel at AED X'
questions.why: Marking guide, task 1. See §8.3 and Exercise 2.

questions.stem: Exercise 2: determine the three execution elements that were missing.
options: Culture alignment, leadership at every level (the supervisors), and communication beyond the video — plus the unspent training budget
questions.why: Marking guide, task 1. See §8.5 and Exercise 2.

questions.stem: Exercise 2: Determine the driving and restraining forces in the warehouse change.
options: Driving: the e-commerce growth strategy, the CEO mandate, younger staff; restraining: supervisors' expertise and habit, no training, remote-depot exclusion, dual paper/digital tolerated
Driving: the remote depots; restraining: younger staff
questions.why: Marking guide, task 2. See §8.7 and Exercise 2.

questions.stem: Exercise 2: determine which Lewin phases the company skipped and the evidence.
options: Unfreezing was skipped (no case for change made to supervisors) and refreezing is absent (paper still accepted)
Changing was skipped — no system exists
Refreezing was complete — paper is gone
questions.why: Marking guide, task 2. See §8.7 and Exercise 2.

questions.stem: Exercise 2: for the supervisors, determine the reason for resistance, what they protect, and the fitting recommendation.
options: Habit and sunk expertise, fear of incompetence — protecting competence; respect the expertise, make them the trainers, training first
questions.why: Marking guide, task 3. See §8.8 and Exercise 2.

questions.stem: Exercise 2: for the remote depots, determine the reason for resistance and the recommendation.
options: Distrust and exclusion — involve them, visit, give equal visibility
questions.why: Marking guide, task 3. See §8.8 and Exercise 2.

questions.stem: Exercise 2: Determine why 'more pressure' from the CEO would fail.
options: Adding driving force raises tension and hardens the informal leaders; reducing restraining forces works with less stress
Pressure works only on young staff
questions.why: Marking guide, task 3. See §8.7 and Exercise 2.

questions.stem: Select the 90-day plan ordering that the marking guide rewards.
options: Week 1: supervisor workshop on the case and the numbers (unfreeze); weeks 2–4: supervisor-led training (change); paper phased out by a date with the exception process removed (refreeze); a monthly adoption-plus-error measure
Week 1: cancel paper; week 2: fire resisters; week 3: new video
Week 1: buy more IT; week 2: announce success
questions.why: Marking guide, task 4. See §8.7 and Exercise 2.

questions.stem: Exercise 2: select the one measure to report to the CEO each month.
options: Adoption plus error rate in the digital system
questions.why: Measurement and correction. See §8.5 and Exercise 2.

questions.stem: Take-away: a student reads a published UAE strategy and finds a vision a front-line employee could not connect to their work. Determine the chapter's verdict.
options: It fails the criteria — a vision must be one a new employee can repeat and recognise their work in
questions.why: Take-away box 1. See §8.2.

questions.stem: Take-away: the strategy document contains no objective that is measurable and dated. Determine what the chapter says that is.
options: A finding — an objective without a number and a date is a wish
A sign of a good vision
questions.why: Take-away box 2. See §8.3.

questions.stem: Take-away: the document covers structure and budget but says nothing about who at middle level translates the strategy into behaviour. Determine the execution element left to someone else.
questions.why: Take-away box 3. See §8.5.

questions.stem: The tunnel collapses and the old plan is useless; Rami must first convince the team that the old route is gone before proposing a new one. Determine the Lewin phase.
options: Unfreezing — make the current state unacceptable so people let go
questions.why: People must let go before they can take hold. See §8.7.

questions.stem: Dana refuses the new cliff route because she has never climbed and fears looking slow in front of the others. Determine what she is protecting and the recommendation.
options: Competence and belonging — reach her individually, pair her with Omar, make the first success visible
questions.why: Answers to questions 3 and 4. See §8.8.

questions.stem: The team has adopted the new route, but Rami keeps rewarding Omar for scouting the old valley. Determine the phase at risk.
options: Refreezing — rewards still support the old way, so the change will slide back
questions.why: Align rewards with the new state. See §8.7.

questions.stem: Rami tells the team 'a valley where every child walks to school without fear'. Classify the statement.
options: A vision — ambitious, memorable, a source of motivation
questions.why: A vision answers WHY. See §8.2.

questions.stem: Rami turns the vision into 'To reach the fortress wall by the third dawn with all four of us uninjured'. Classify it.
options: An objective — specific, measurable, single result, target date
questions.why: To + verb + result + date. See §8.3.

questions.stem: Rami wins the villagers' support by first freeing the mill from the gang — a small, visible success. Determine the role element.
questions.why: The strategic leader's role in change. See §8.6.

questions.stem: Noor lists what the gang does well and badly, and what the party can and cannot do, before Rami chooses to strike at the water supply. Classify the step.
options: Strategy formulation — matching internal strengths to external opportunities, then the courage to choose
questions.why: Analysis before the plan; formulation is the choice. See §8.4.

questions.stem: The plan is agreed but nobody checks each night whether the party is on schedule; by day three they are a day behind and nobody knows. Determine the execution element missing.
questions.why: Nobody measures, so nobody knows it has failed. See §8.5.

questions.stem: Rami's village council writes 'to protect every traveller on the valley road, from any village, with the fastest riders in the hills'. Classify the statement.
questions.why: Mission criteria. See §8.2.

questions.stem: The gang changes tactics; Rami notices the pattern before the first raid and starts preparing the villages. Determine the role element.
options: Anticipating the need for change before the crisis
questions.why: The strategic leader's role in change. See §8.6.

questions.stem: Rami improves the night-watch rota a little each week within the same defence plan. Classify the change and how it is led.
options: Incremental change — led mostly transactionally through objectives and rewards
questions.why: Two kinds of change. See §8.6.

questions.stem: Rami replaces the whole defence with a new alliance of villages, a new structure and new rewards for courage. Classify the change and how it is led.
options: Transformational change — led transformationally through vision and commitment
questions.why: Two kinds of change. See §8.6.

questions.stem: Rami studies the gang's new weapons and the valley's new road (external) and the team's exhaustion (internal) before choosing where to strike. Determine the two analyses.
options: External analysis — opportunities and threats; internal analysis — strengths and weaknesses
questions.why: Formulation matches the two. See §8.4.

questions.stem: Noor's analysis is perfect but Rami refuses to choose a plan until he is certain. Determine the chapter's point.
options: Formulation is a leadership act — it requires the courage to choose under uncertainty, which no analysis supplies
questions.why: Formulation — the strategic leader's choice. See §8.4.

questions.stem: Determine what the Google case shows about formulation.
options: The strategy followed the analysis, but betting the company before the evidence was complete was the leadership
questions.why: The Google case. See §8.4.
